from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["A sharp clap is quick.", "A steady hum persists.", "Signals exist in time or frequency."]
        self.setup_layout("Intuitive Hook: The Musical Note", lecture_lines)
        
        # Initialize objects
        wave = FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.sin(2 * PI * x), x_range=[-1, 1], color=WHITE)
        freq_label = Text("Frequency", font_size=24, color="#FF0000")
        
        # Place initially
        self.place_at_grid(wave, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(freq_label, 'B3', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"), Create(wave))
        self.play(FadeIn(freq_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        # Scale the wave to visualize higher frequency (change amplitude/freq in a simple way)
        new_wave = FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.sin(4 * PI * x), x_range=[-1, 1], color=WHITE)
        new_wave.move_to(wave.get_center())
        self.play(Transform(wave, new_wave))
        self.play(freq_label.animate.set_color("#00FF00"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#0000FF"))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(wave), FadeOut(freq_label), FadeOut(self.lecture), FadeOut(self.title))

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Prerequisite: The Fourier Transform", [
            "Fourier Transform acts like a prism.",
            "It reveals constituent frequencies of signals.",
            "A pulse narrows in time."

        kernel = formula[0][6:11]
        self.play(kernel.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Time and frequency widths are reciprocal.", "Widths are linked by a constant.", "This is an inherent wave property.", "Shrink time, frequency side grows.", "The balance is mathematically enforced."]
        self.setup_layout("The Core Concept: The Reciprocal Relationship", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup visual elements
        time_bar = Rectangle(height=0.5, width=4, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.6)
        freq_bar = Rectangle(height=0.5, width=4, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.6)
        
        self.place_at_grid(time_bar, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(freq_bar, "E2")
        
        time_label = Text("Δt", font_size=24).next_to(time_bar, LEFT)
        freq_label = Text("Δf", font_size=24).next_to(freq_bar, LEFT)
        
        constant_label = MathTex(r"\Delta t \cdot \Delta f \geq C", font_size=32, color=GREEN).move_to(self.grid["D4"])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), Write(time_bar), Write(freq_bar), Write(time_label), Write(freq_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN), Write(constant_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(BLUE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Shrink time_bar, grow freq_bar
        new_time_width = 1.5
        new_freq_width = 6.0
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"),
            time_bar.animate.set_width(new_time_width),
            freq_bar.animate.set_width(new_freq_width),
            run_time=2
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Uncertainty Principle: The Fourier Trade-off

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Musical Note
sections.content: Introduce the concept that a sound can be defined either by 'when' it happens (time) or 'what pitch' it has (frequency). Explain that these two representations are linked via the Fourier Transform.
sections.example: A short, sharp clap versus a long, steady hum of a tuning fork.

sections.title: Mathematical Prerequisite: The Fourier Transform
sections.content: Briefly define the Fourier Transform as a prism that breaks a signal down into its constituent frequencies. Visualize this as a transition from a wave packet in the time domain to a distribution curve in the frequency domain.
sections.example: Animation showing a time-domain pulse narrowing while the corresponding frequency spectrum spreads out.

sections.title: The Core Concept: The Reciprocal Relationship
sections.content: Explain that the width of the signal in time (Δt) and the width of the signal in frequency (Δf) are inversely proportional. Mathematically: Δt * Δf ≥ Constant. Emphasize that this is not a measurement error, but an inherent property of waves.
sections.example: A 'Time-Frequency Seesaw': As one side shrinks, the other must grow to balance the equation.

sections.title: Physical Application: Heisenberg’s Analogy
sections.content: Connect the Fourier Uncertainty Principle to quantum mechanics. Since a particle is described by a wave function, the exact same mathematical constraint applies to its position (x) and momentum (p).
sections.example: A 'Quantum Cat' metaphor: If you pinpoint a cat's exact location in a room, you lose all information about its velocity (momentum).

sections.title: Summary & Reflection
sections.content: Reiterate that 'Uncertainty' is a fundamental feature of the universe. Conclude by linking signal processing to quantum physics, reinforcing that the Fourier Transform is the universal language for this trade-off.
sections.example: Review of the 'Clap vs. Hum' example: Why you cannot perfectly identify the exact moment a beat occurs while also knowing its precise pitch.
